text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures reversed a steady decline from the middle of last week as German inflation reports calmed worries that prices here were climbing. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.34, up 0.11 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended higher on Tuesday after a day spent idling in narrow ranges as many investors stuck to the sidelines ahead of Wednesday's auction and speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-2/32, up 2/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures failed to break out of the narrow range they've been stuck in since last week and traders saw a similar trend continuing ahead of remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday. The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.24, up 0.12. from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures slipped lower in late afternoon on profit-taking after investors turned cautious and the lira slipped further against the German mark. Dealers said that there were still uncertainty that an agreement could be hammered out between the government and the Communists over the planned 1997 mini-budget. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.48 down 0.71 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened higher on Tuesday but analysts foresaw another session of narrow-ranged trading before Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-23/32, up 3/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.65 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended firmer on Tuesday on short-covering that emerged toward the close. Comments made by Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama that the interest rate gap between Japan and other countries should be narrowed invited some selling early in the afternoon, but the impact was limited overall. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.17, up 0.11 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - Dollar Eurobonds were the main focus on Tuesday, with short-dated paper the most popular.
"Demand at the moment is for dollar bonds at five years or less," said a syndicate manager at a European bank.
